sources.title: Fears for future as South Korea's fertility rate drops again
sources.limits: Use only as one published tally; chapter keeps a range because cumulative totals differ by source and definition.

sources.title: Korean Policies to Reverse the Decline in the Fertility Rate, Part 1
sources.limits: Think-tank analysis; do not infer causal effectiveness from spending totals alone.

sources.title: Every baby in 2024 comes with W29.6m cash support
supports: approximately 29.6 million won combined per-child support level in 2024
sources.limits: Single-year benefit snapshot; not a measure of lifetime policy cost or causal fertility effect.

sources.title: Hungary's Fertility Outcomes Highlight Pro-Natal Policy Limitations
supports: TFR rise followed by later decline
sources.limits: Policy commentary rather than causal identification; use to frame limitations, not to prove policy failure.

sources.title: Is Hungary Experiencing a Policy-Induced Baby Boom?
supports: academic estimates of additional births associated with policy changes
sources.limits: Blog-format synthesis; preserve uncertainty around causality and tempo effects.

sources.title: Migration and Demographic Challenges: New Policy Approaches in Japan and Germany
supports: comparative Japan/Germany aging and migration-policy framing
sources.limits: Use national statistical agencies for current headcounts and election authorities for political results.

sources.title: Foreign residents at end of 2025
sources.publisher: Immigration Services Agency of Japan (released March 27, 2026)
sources.limits: Foreign-resident growth demonstrates migration-policy adaptation but does not by itself measure net fiscal effects, integration quality, or whether migration offsets aging at national scale.

sources.title: As Its Population Ages, Japan Quietly Turns to Immigration
sources.limits: Use current ISA data for resident counts; worker-shortfall projections vary by model and year.

sources.title: 2025 Bundestag election: final result
sources.publisher: The Federal Returning Officer of Germany (Mar. 14, 2025)
supports: AfD won 20.8% of valid second votes in the 2025 Bundestag election
sources.limits: Election result establishes vote share, not a single causal explanation for why voters supported the party.

sources.title: Ishiba's LDP Coalition Loses Majority in Japan's Upper House Election
supports: party campaigned on a Japanese First platform
ruling coalition lost its upper-house majority
sources.limits: Election outcome demonstrates a political constraint but does not prove immigration was the dominant determinant of voting behavior.

sources.title: Old-age dependency ratio
supports: historical and projected old-age dependency ratios across OECD economies
sources.limits: Projection, not certainty; migration, labor-force participation, retirement age, and productivity can change fiscal effects.

sources.title: The Rise of the Silver Economy: Global Implications of Aging (WEO Chapter 2)
supports: aging and dependency-ratio pressures on potential output
mitigating roles for migration, labor participation, and productivity
sources.limits: Macroeconomic assessment, not a deterministic forecast for any single country.

sources.title: Silver Human Resource Center system overview
supports: approximately 1,300 centers and 700,000+ members at time of report
sources.limits: Historical snapshot; current participation should be rechecked before using precise present-tense totals.

sources.title: Act on Stabilization of Employment of Elderly Persons (2020 amendment)
sources.publisher: Japanese Law Translation / Ministry of Justice
supports: best-efforts duty to secure employment opportunities up to age 70, effective April 2021
sources.limits: Duty of effort, not a binding individual employment guarantee.
